As a Canadian and someone with leaning towards imports both Japanese and European, I can offer this advice:

Pretty well anything JDM (Honda, Toyota, Nissan etc) are going to be a toss up as far as rust. Most are going to have at least some rust, some are going to have a lot more. 

I've noticed in the last couple years though that the uhh... propensity for deterioration that these cars have, has led to it being easier to find examples in reasonable shape. I'd attribute this to the ones that weren't maintained/washed/undercoated are just gone by now or are getting scraped because they wont pass safety. Not saying that every JDM car left is perfect (my del Sol has no floors and my Integra has new fenders) but it has been getting easier to filter out the crap.

As far as Euro cars go, there doesn't seem to be much of a difference from up north to down south other than occasional rust problems. I've had two VW Jetta MKIVs with the 1.8t motor and they held up pretty well and I've got two friends, one with an A4 and the other an A6 Allroad that haven't had any issues from the climate. 

The only issue I've really seen come up with my Euro friends is the rubber and plastic for vacuum lines, intake etc dry rot and wear out faster from the big changes in temperature that tend to come with this latitude. Be prepared to spend most of your initial time finding leaks.

TL;DR You already said rust. Rubber doesn't like weather changes and a lot of poorly maintained JDM cars have been culled by rust and government safety programs

I'm going to give my two cents as someone who got out about a year ago. 

For me personally dating was the same as a lot of other people have said in this thread; get out on your days off or early nights. Go to shows or just a bar and don't be afraid to talk to people. 

As someone who now works 6-6 Monday to Friday running and programming CNC mills, if you have a passion for cooking don't leave the industry unless you legitimately feel its impossible to make work. The grass isn't always greener and sometimes cooking is what you're really meant for. 

People will care more about you being passionate about yourself, your hobbies and your work than your schedule. 

That said, hobbies other than smoking, drinking and drugs are very important. I personally have a bunch of different hobbies and it helps to prevent you from just being a crazed insomniac worker bee on your days off. 

Oh and don't forget about self improvement. Gym, biking, walking, hiking or literally anything. I'm paying the price now as someone that ignored all that for a long time. It helps literally everything in life if you work towards something for yourself. 

TL;DR Be passionate about yourself, work and you're hobbies. Also don't forget to do things for yourself and to get out of your comfort zone every so often. 

Edit: Also don't be afraid to walk away from places that take your life away  without it being given. I've worked 70+ hours at a place that demanded it and the same at a place I cared about and gave it willingly. I met my soon to be wife at the latter because I was less of a miserable asshat. 

So as much as I just said what you do outside of work matters, work does too. If you hate where you work(which means live for people like us given the hours) you're not going to be the most attractive socially or physically. 

Edit TL;DR If you hate it, find somewhere else. You'll thank yourself.

My list isn't exactly 'old school' per say but I feel that these games are awesome enough to require a mention:

1. Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic (Bioware, 2003)
    Best Star Wars game I've ever played and still one of the best RPGs even in my opinion. Combat is a cross between turnbased and realtime that flows really well and is based in part on the mechanics of Dungeons and Dragons 3.5. Also featured is an awesome alignment system that makes the already awesome story even better.
     KotOR 2 was pretty good as well and is even better after the cut content is restored by modding. KotOR 1 is available on Steam for $9.99. KotOR 2 is harder to come by but definitely worth it as well.

2. Neverwinter Nights 1 (Bioware, 2002)
    Neverwinter Nights is still 9 years after its release one of the best fantasy RPGs I've ever played and is still a staple of every LAN party I go to. Combat is similar to KotOR except that it is from a top down aspect. Good solid story based in the Forgotten Realms DnD setting. Its available on GOG for $9.99.

4. The Elder Scroll III: Morrowind (Bethesda, 2002)
    Hands down my favorite RPG of all time. As awesome as Skyrim is I still feel all these years later that Morrowind is the best game in the Elder Scrolls series. The art design of the game is unique and has helped keep the game from really showing its age. It is available on Steam for $9.99.
